It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. div.head: ECf retr 18
div.ab: De reis lege dampnatis ad misericordiam regis recurrentibus. Tamen si quispiam forisfactus poposcerit regis misericordiam pro forisfacto suo, timidus mortis uel membrorum perdendorum, potest ei rex lege sue dignitatis condonare, si uult, etiam mortem promeritam.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 643 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

div.ab: Of the guilty, condemned by law, who have recourse to the king's mercy. Yet if anyone who has committed an offence begs the king's mercy for his offence, fearful of death or of losing limbs, the king can pardon him by the law of his dignity, if he wishes, even a death deserved.
